statement: A reviewer can inspect all proposed test cases, steps, assertions, six-domain mappings, runner choices, and evidence requirements before any case executes.
Verification is blocked until the current case snapshot has explicit user approval.
Every change follows the full Verification 2.0 gate; no request can select a light, compact, or simplified verification path.
The runtime setup command installs the locked Verification Runtime outside the business repository and shows exact installed versions and browser status.
Runtime doctor reports missing Node, packages, browser binaries, Midscene provider configuration, corrupt locks, and permission failures as exact blockers.
A reviewer can see first failure, retry, repair, retest, and regression attempts without earlier evidence being overwritten.
A retry that passes is labeled FLAKY; a repaired case that passes is labeled PASS AFTER FIX.
overview.html shows lifecycle readiness, six-domain status, blocker counts, freshness, integrity, repair-loop state, and release verdict.
test-case-catalog.html shows the approved case contract and domain coverage.
test-case-results.html shows runs, attempts, readings, commands, evidence, hashes, freshness, and repair history.
Green, red, blocked, running, canceled, stale, flaky, and pass-after-fix reports share the same navigation and information hierarchy.
Report pages work on desktop and mobile, are keyboard operable, and preserve verdict and evidence information in print output.
Versioned schemas validate test cases, approvals, snapshots, runs, attempts, readings, evidence, indexes, failures, runtime, reports, and gates.
Every attempt is bound to change id, case id, run id, attempt id, code SHA, test SHA, scenario hash, environment hash, browser project, and test data snapshot.
Retry is rejected when any retry identity fingerprint changes.
Midscene output cannot produce PASS without a deterministic assertion, structured fact, or explicit human signoff.
Missing evidence files, hash mismatch, size mismatch, stale SHA, unrecognized producer, or broken case/step references block green.
Empty evidence arrays, empty verification commands, or a manually edited green domain report cannot produce green.
All six domains receive a terminal result for every approved case.
not_applicable requires a reason, evidence, reviewer identity, approval timestamp, and policy allowance.
Domain status and release verdict are derived from case readings; no domain skill or agent prose can override the aggregate.
Raw evidence is append-only, the summary index is rebuildable, and cache loss does not lose source truth.
Case-level freshness uses SHA and execution fingerprints rather than mtime alone.
Rerun scope returns concrete affected case ids and reasons, not only domain names.
A failed case creates a frozen failure packet and routes product or test repair to a standard development task packet.
Regression scope includes the repaired case, directly impacted cases, and policy-required baseline cases.
Repeated no-progress repair attempts route to break-loop governance instead of silently retrying.
Release and archive block on unapproved cases, incomplete readings, stale or tampered evidence, open failures, missing reports, or red or blocked gates.
Reports generate for green, red, and blocked states and never become the source of truth.
HTML rendering escapes artifact content and never exposes provider secrets.
Evidence records contain stable id, kind, path, hash, size, producer, timestamp, change, run, case, attempt, step or assertion, code SHA, and test SHA.
Failed evidence is retained after retry, repair, migration, report regeneration, release, and archive.
V1-to-V2 migration provides dry-run output, backup references, migration receipt, validation results, and rollback instructions.
Migration never interprets missing V1 evidence as V2 PASS.
Gate decisions name source case readings, evidence index version, runtime version, kernel version, and freshness result.
One host-neutral Verification Kernel owns schemas, state transitions, evidence integrity, aggregation, freshness, and report model semantics.
Codex, Claude Code, and CodeFree-O adapters pass the same kernel contract and fixture suite.
Shared report components are reused across all three HTML pages.
Playwright, Midscene, command execution, EvidenceStore, failure classification, and report rendering use explicit adapter or service boundaries.
Duplicate verification logic across host repositories is removed or replaced by generated or synchronized kernel consumption with drift detection.
